reference.source: Parsons' Diseases of the Eye 23rd Edition (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: Blanch test separates episclera from sclera
White eye with vision loss: posterior scleritis
Blue sclera plus fractures: osteogenesis imperfecta
reference.pathophysiology: Immune complex vasculitis occludes deep episcleral plexuses, ischaemiating scleral collagen into necrosis, while posterior inflammation oozes into sub Tenon space outlining the T; collagen dysplasias thin sclera congenitally letting uveal pigment blue through.
additionalDifferentials: Episcleritis versus scleritis by blanching and tenderness
Necrotising with versus without inflammation by pain and redness
Posterior scleritis versus tumour by T sign and systemic clues
additionalInvestigations: Phenylephrine blanching test at slit lamp
Autoimmune, ANCA, infective and chest workup
B scan for T sign in suspected posterior disease
